principles: Audit-only provenance: signatureTag + signatureTagSource never touch the finding _hash, signFinding, or any gate.
Reuse the existing registry primitives (resolveTag) rather than new storage.
Honest fallback: the mechanical candidate is a non-empty fallback, not a claim of human-quality signatures.
Pure derivation: the candidate function is deterministic and I/O-free.
Byte-identical confirmed path: a reviewer-supplied tag behaves exactly as today, only gaining source=confirmed.
drivers: Must not perturb the finding _hash or the REVIEW->TEST findings gate (finding.ts is gate-critical).
Must give the ③.5 backfill a provenance flag to distinguish/upgrade auto vs confirmed.
Must populate a tag for every finding so learning_scan signals are never empty by omission.

options.name: Auto-candidate fallback at finding_add + source flag (chosen)
pros: Smallest change to a gate-critical handler; mirrors the existing signatureTag exclusion.
Pure leaf for the derivation keeps it testable and deterministic.
Provenance flag is exactly what the ③.5 backfill and future weighting need.
cons: Mechanical candidates are degraded (acceptable: they are an explicit fallback; quality comes from confirmed tags).

options.name: Require reviewers to always supply a signatureTag
cons: Adds reviewer burden + a new blocking requirement; inconsistent across reviewers.
Findings filed by non-reviewer paths would have no tag.

options.name: Derive signatures only later in learning_scan (not at finding_add)
cons: No provenance captured at source; cannot distinguish confirmed vs auto.
The backfill would have nothing to upgrade; loses the forward confirmed-tag path.

chosen: Auto-candidate fallback at finding_add + source flag (chosen)
rationale: Capturing the candidate + provenance at finding_add is the only place that distinguishes a reviewer-confirmed tag from a machine fallback, which is exactly what the ③.5 backfill and any future weighting require; the change to the gate-critical handler is minimal and mirrors the existing audit-only signatureTag exclusion, and the derivation lives in a pure testable leaf. The alternatives either add reviewer burden or lose provenance.

preMortem.scenario: The new fields change the finding _hash and break the findings gate.
preMortem.trigger: signatureTagSource (or a re-ordered signatureTag) gets included in the object signFinding hashes.
preMortem.consequence: Every finding's signature changes; the REVIEW->TEST findings gate and any signature-bound evidence break.
preMortem.mitigation: Exclude both fields from signFinding exactly as signatureTag is excluded today; the smoke + verifier assert the finding _hash is byte-identical with vs without the new fields (the single most important check).

preMortem.scenario: The auto-candidate is mistaken for a high-quality signature.
preMortem.trigger: Downstream code treats source=auto tags as equal to confirmed, inflating apparent signal quality.
preMortem.consequence: Effectiveness metrics / the backfill over-credit degraded machine signatures (the Baseline-A trap).
preMortem.mitigation: signatureTagSource explicitly marks provenance; this story does NOT weight them (deferred) but records the flag so ③.4/③.5 can treat confirmed > auto and the backfill can upgrade auto->confirmed.

preMortem.trigger: Refactoring the signatureTag handling changes behavior when a reviewer DOES supply a tag.
preMortem.consequence: Existing reviewer-tagged findings behave differently; hint/registry hints break.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep the supplied-tag branch byte-identical except for adding source=confirmed; the smoke asserts a supplied tag is stored unchanged with source=confirmed.

preMortem.scenario: The candidate derivation does I/O or is non-deterministic.
preMortem.trigger: deriveSignatureCandidate reads the registry file or uses time/randomness.
preMortem.consequence: finding_add gains hidden I/O / non-determinism; tests flake.
preMortem.mitigation: The leaf imports only node:/types and is a pure function of (category, files, desc); any registry alias folding happens in the handler via resolveTag, not the leaf; the smoke asserts determinism.
